-- Seed the `works_at` auto_create_when rule on every public catalog org.
--
-- The identity engine (packages/server/src/identity/engine.ts) derives a
-- relationship edge when a person-fact's normalized value equals a catalog
-- entity's `metadata->>targetField`. This migration wires the canonical
-- employment inference:
--
--   person fact  email_domain = "acme.com"
--   catalog company  metadata.domain = "acme.com"
--   ⇒ derive  person --works_at--> company
--
-- The `email_domain` fact is derived centrally by the engine from every
-- `email` fact (see deriveCompanionFacts), so this fires for any connector
-- that produces an email — not just Google Workspace `hd` sign-ins.
--
-- Two things must be true for the engine to act (both seeded here, per
-- public-catalog org that has a `company` type):
--   1. `company.domain` is declared `x-identity-namespace: true` in the type's
--      metadata_schema — engine.ts:findEntitiesByMetadataField refuses to match
--      an undeclared field.
--   2. an active `works_at` relationship type carries the compiled rule blob
--      { autoCreateWhen, ruleVersion, ruleHash } in `metadata`.
--
-- ruleHash below is sha256 of the canonicalised rule set, matching
-- ruleHashFor() in packages/server/src/identity/rules.ts. It is validated at
-- read time by loadRules(): if this hash ever disagrees with a fresh hash of
-- the stored rules (e.g. the canonicaliser changes), the engine SKIPS the rule
-- and logs drift rather than acting on a stale rule — so a mistake here fails
-- safe (no derivations), never wrong. If the rule set is edited, recompute the
-- hash with ruleHashFor and reseed.
--
-- assuranceRequired = 'oauth_verified': only provider-verified emails derive an
-- edge. A self-attested or scraped contact email will not create a works_at,
-- and a personal @gmail.com never matches a company (gmail.com is not a
-- company domain), so false "works at Google" edges are avoided by design.
--
-- matchStrategy = 'unique_only': if two catalog companies share a domain the
-- engine records a collision event for human resolution instead of guessing.

DO $$
DECLARE
  org RECORD;
  company_type RECORD;
  schema jsonb;
  props jsonb;
  domain_prop jsonb;
  rule_metadata jsonb;
BEGIN
  rule_metadata := jsonb_build_object(
    'autoCreateWhen', jsonb_build_array(
      jsonb_build_object(
        'sourceNamespace', 'email_domain',
        'targetField', 'domain',
        'assuranceRequired', 'oauth_verified',
        'matchStrategy', 'unique_only'
      )
    ),
    'ruleVersion', 1,
    'ruleHash', 'db3256f51ec866accb213b0167068f2f4df32e55b4bd5eb83067d27a157c7419'
  );

  FOR org IN
    SELECT id FROM organization WHERE visibility = 'public'
  LOOP
    -- Only orgs that actually model companies get the rule/field.
    SELECT id, metadata_schema INTO company_type
    FROM entity_types
    WHERE organization_id = org.id
      AND slug = 'company'
      AND deleted_at IS NULL
    LIMIT 1;

    IF NOT FOUND THEN
      CONTINUE;
    END IF;

    -- 1. Declare company.domain as an identity-matchable field, preserving any
    --    existing schema/props. Only ADD the marker when it is absent — an
    --    existing x-identity-namespace value (true OR the richer object form the
    --    engine also accepts) is left untouched, so a reseed never downgrades a
    --    hand-tuned declaration. Idempotent: with the marker present this is a
    --    no-op on that key.
    schema := COALESCE(company_type.metadata_schema, '{"type":"object"}'::jsonb);
    props := COALESCE(schema -> 'properties', '{}'::jsonb);
    domain_prop := COALESCE(props -> 'domain', '{"type":"string"}'::jsonb);
    IF NOT (domain_prop ? 'x-identity-namespace') THEN
      domain_prop := domain_prop || '{"x-identity-namespace": true}'::jsonb;
      props := props || jsonb_build_object('domain', domain_prop);
      schema := schema || jsonb_build_object('properties', props);
      UPDATE entity_types
      SET metadata_schema = schema, updated_at = now()
      WHERE id = company_type.id;
    END IF;

    -- 2. Upsert the works_at type carrying the compiled rule. Idempotent on the
    --    active (organization_id, slug) unique index; on conflict we MERGE the
    --    rule keys into any existing metadata (never clobber other fields on an
    --    already-defined works_at type) so a reseed corrects drift in place.
    INSERT INTO entity_relationship_types (
      organization_id, slug, name, description, is_symmetric, status, metadata,
      created_at, updated_at
    ) VALUES (
      org.id, 'works_at', 'Works at',
      'Person is employed by / affiliated with a company. Auto-derived when the person''s email domain matches the company''s domain.',
      false, 'active', rule_metadata, now(), now()
    )
    ON CONFLICT (organization_id, slug) WHERE (status = 'active')
    DO UPDATE SET
      metadata = COALESCE(entity_relationship_types.metadata, '{}'::jsonb) || rule_metadata,
      updated_at = now();
  END LOOP;
END $$;

## Verdict

The plan has two good deletions, but its central premise is wrong: **org-scoped `$member` identities cannot replace the global platform-principal → Lobu-user mapping** without either losing features or adding a new global identity system. As written, it is net-complexity and would weaken ACL safety.

I fetched `origin/main`; PR #2411 is **OPEN**, not shipped.

### 1. Claims that are wrong / incomplete

- **`entity_identities` is not written only by entity-link-upsert and access-graph.** It is also written by member provisioning, sign-in adoption, `save_content`, canvas creation, keyed-entity promotion, and merge operations.  
  `packages/server/src/auth/subject-identities.ts:60-70,107-128`  
  `packages/server/src/utils/member-entity.ts:136-144`  
  `packages/server/src/tools/save_content.ts:326-335`  
  `packages/server/src/utils/canvas-events.ts:161-170`  
  `packages/server/src/utils/promote-keyed-entities.ts:424-433`  
  Its live uniqueness claim is correct: `db/migrations/00000000000000_baseline.sql:3674-3678`.

- **“Adoption happens only at sign-in” is too strong.** It is Slack-only (`subject-identities.ts:315`), but it is invoked from BetterAuth `account.create.after` *and* `account.update.after`, which includes account linking/refresh lifecycle events, not only an initial sign-in.  
  `packages/server/src/auth/index.tsx:858-898,901-936`.

- **`/lobu link` is not merely an RBAC helper.** `chat_user_identities` is read for:
  - in-chat builder-admin grants: `gateway/orchestration/message-consumer.ts:123-143`
  - Slack approval authorization: `gateway/connections/interaction-bridge.ts:132-171`
  - re-binding an agent without a new code: `gateway/commands/built-in-commands.ts:205-232`
  - Slack App Home’s cross-org notification inbox: `gateway/connections/chat-instance-manager.ts:177-229`
  - owner-DM notification routing: `notifications/service.ts:161-202`
  - Slack install claiming before an org has been selected: `gateway/connections/slack-claim-identities.ts:12-75`.

  It is true that the **channel recall gate** does not read this table. But that does not make deletion safe.

- **The identity-fact engine is not “read via JOIN at `auth-hook.ts:90,149`.”** Those joins resolve a trusted `$member` from `auth_user_id`; they are inputs to engine scheduling, not readers of `identity_fact` outputs.  
  `packages/server/src/identity/auth-hook.ts:78-116,139-169`.  
  The engine does write fact events and derived relationship rows: `identity/engine.ts:429-441,662-798`. Those `works_at` derivations are explicitly seeded by migration: `db/migrations/20260707120000_seed_works_at_email_domain_rule.sql:1-132`.

- **“Telegram / X / Discord mint nothing” is only true for `sender-identity.ts`.** That module has Slack only: `gateway/connections/sender-identity.ts:39-60`; Telegram messages do carry author ID/name into transcript capture: `message-handler-bridge.ts:884-904`.  
  But:
  - X already mints `x_user_id` / `x_handle` entities through connector attribution, not chat transcripts: `packages/connectors/src/x.ts:160-204`.
  - Discord is an actual chat platform (`platforms/index.ts:19-27`) but has no sender-identity mapping.
  - A Telegram user who uses `/link` can already receive a global `chat_user_identities` row; “no identity row at all” is false. `lobu/stores/chat-identity.ts:7-22,60-78`.

- **The hollow-name issue is real but conditional.** ACL sync creates the raw `T:U` title because `slackChannelsToResources()` sets `name: combined`; `resolveMembers()` uses that as `display_name`/`titlePath`.  
  `packages/connectors/src/slack-identity.ts:151-172`  
  `packages/server/src/authz/access-graph.ts:190-214`.  
  The resource refresh exists only for resources: `access-graph.ts:332-350`. A transcript received first can mint a person using the actual chat author name, so it is not universal; ACL-first entities remain stale.

- **Slack email is not fetched.** Both declared scope lists lack `users:read.email`; `origin/main` has no `users.list` implementation. The Slack Web client only implements `users.info`, which does not expose profile email in its typed result.  
  `packages/connectors/src/slack.ts:41-69`  
  `config/slack-app-manifest.self-install.json:35-70`  
  `gateway/connections/slack-web.ts:15-110,197-208`.  
  `member_joined_channel` is subscribed but has no handler; after a fresh fetch, its only `origin/main` occurrences are those two declarations.

- **The merge claim is correct.** Cross-type merges throw: `utils/entity-merge.ts:210-214`.

- **The channel-visibility short-circuit claim is correct**, as is the type mismatch in a naïve union. `byAuth` takes a BetterAuth user ID while the fallback expects a platform user ID: `authz/channel-visibility.ts:100-164`.  
  Important qualification: the fallback does **not** restrict the owner to `$member`; it can return a `person`. `channel-visibility.ts:123-135`. The web/resource gate does require `$member`: `authz/resource-visibility.ts:99-126`.

- **PR #2411 is not present in this checkout/main.** Current `resolveMembers()` still picks the first matching identity in input order: `authz/access-graph.ts:134-217`. PR #2411 is open and is precisely the intended primary-tier repair.

### 2. Step 8: email as an additional **primary** is unsafe

**Do not do this.**

On current `main`, it is already unsafe because `resolveMembers()` uses first-match order, not `primary`: `access-graph.ts:173-184`.

After PR #2411, it is still unsafe if email is marked primary. Its proposed logic collects all primary hits, then resolves when there is exactly one hit. Therefore:

```text
fresh slack_user_id → no hit
recycled/shared email → existing $member hit
=> exactly one primary hit
=> resolve to email holder
```

That is exactly the recycled-identity collapse #2411 prevents for a stable primary plus a secondary claim.

The correct policy is:

- `slack_user_id` remains the **only primary**.
- Slack email is, at most, a **secondary enrichment field**, not an adoption key.
- If a fresh Slack ID has no owner, mint a new `person`; do not collapse it onto an email holder.
- Later move it to `$member` only with a stronger proof: Slack OIDC identity or an explicitly accepted `/lobu link` capability.

Also, the `entity-link-upsert.ts:756-780` semantics you cite do not currently protect `access-graph`; #2411 is what aligns access-graph with them.

### 3. Deleting `chat_user_identities` is not safe

Its global scope encodes a real, different invariant:

```text
(platform, team_id, platform_user_id) → one global Lobu user
```

The PK enforces that globally: `baseline.sql:655-663,2744-2749`. In contrast, `entity_identities` permits the same platform identity to point to different entities in different orgs: its unique key includes `organization_id`: `baseline.sql:3674-3678`.

For one human in several orgs DMing a bot:

- the current table resolves the human once, then the target org determines their role;
- Slack App Home deliberately uses that global identity to show notifications spanning all their orgs: `chat-instance-manager.ts:177-229`;
- an org-scoped graph claim cannot answer that query without searching every org and facing ambiguity;
- it also loses the current hard protection against the same Slack principal being assigned to different Lobu users in different orgs.

Slack Grid worsens this: current callers deliberately try both workspace `T…` and enterprise `E…` keys: `message-consumer.ts:123-143`.

So either:

1. **Keep the table**. It is a small, correct global-user-identity projection, not redundant graph data; or
2. **Delete the capabilities that require global platform identity**: App Home inbox, reusable link ownership, Slack approval actions, owner-DM routing, and pre-org install claim lookup.

Replacing it with a renamed global `user_identities` table is not simplification.

### 4. Deleting `packages/server/src/identity/` wholesale is unsafe

Deleting the **fact engine** is feasible if losing `identity_fact`, collision events, and derived `works_at` edges is intentional. But deleting the whole directory breaks unrelated required code:

- connector namespace normalization and recall namespaces:  
  `identity/connector-identity-modules.ts:1-63`  
  used by `utils/entity-link-upsert.ts:30` and `utils/content-search/entity-link.ts:9`.
- startup recall-index invariant:  
  `server.ts:50` and `identity/recall-index-invariant.ts:1-89`.
- relationship-rule compilation used by the schema management tool:  
  `tools/admin/manage_entity_schema.ts:34`.
- `resolveMemberOrgsForUser`, used by Slack identity adoption:  
  `auth/subject-identities.ts:11-15`.

The fact engine itself also has a prohibited multi-replica in-memory `Map` lock: `identity/lock.ts:20-66`. Deleting that engine is a simplification win, but first retain/move the non-engine pieces and remove the relationship-rule UI/migration in the same concern.

Existing fact events must not be deleted; `events` is append-only. Stop producing them; tombstone derived relationships if needed; leave history.

### 5. Simplification count

As written, this adds at least **seven mechanisms**:

1. generic multi-namespace adoption;
2. trusted-proof policy for each namespace;
3. Slack directory sync / pagination via `users.list`;
4. profile → ACL-member data model expansion;
5. special cross-type `person → $member` merge/tombstone semantics;
6. Telegram identity namespace/normalizer/attribution policy;
7. member-name refresh/ownership policy.

It deletes:

1. one Slack-specific adopter, replaced by a more general one;
2. the fact engine, if its features are intentionally removed;
3. potentially the chat table—but only by adding a global replacement or deleting several product capabilities.

So: **not a simplification**. The replacements for steps 4, 6, 8, and 9 are where complexity grows.

### 6. Correct order / PR boundaries

1. **Merge PR #2411 first.** It is open, not shipped. Do not add email identities until the primary-tier behavior and tests are on `main`.

2. **Separate PR: delete the identity-fact engine.**  
   Remove scheduling from `auth/index.tsx`, engine/capability/Google-fact code, rule management, seeded `works_at` rule, and related tests. Preserve/move connector normalization, recall invariant, and member-org lookup.

3. **Make the global-vs-org identity decision before any `chat_user_identities` work.**  
   My recommendation: retain it. If the decision is to remove it, make that a product-deletion PR, not a “repoint readers” PR.

4. **Separate Slack profile enrichment PR.**  
   Add scope in both connector declaration and manifest; add a paginated Slack directory API; batch once per team per ACL sync; use it for names. Keep Slack ID as sole primary. Test profile-fetch failure separately from membership-fetch failure.

5. **Separate Slack adoption / cross-type lifecycle PR.**  
   Do not generalize until there is a second provider with a specific verified identifier and normalization contract. Decide whether old `person` rows remain, or implement a real person→member merge that moves edges, emits merge-operation audit data, and sets `merged_into`. A bare `merged_into` update is insufficient: `applyMerge()` moves edges and tombstones the loser as one transaction: `entity-merge.ts:253-347`.

6. **Separate Telegram transcript attribution PR.**  
   This is independent and should be honest about scope: it improves `channel_messages.author_entity_id`; it does not authenticate or attach the sender to a `$member`.

7. **Never schedule the chat-table deletion unless step 3 explicitly chooses product deletion.** It must be last.

### 7. Sharpest structural criticism

You are conflating two graphs:

- **global authentication identity:** “this Slack/Telegram principal is Lobu user X”;
- **org-local authorization/knowledge identity:** “in org O, user X is represented by `$member` M, which may belong to channel C.”

`entity_identities` is deliberately the latter. It is incapable of enforcing a global platform-principal ownership invariant because its unique key is org-scoped. A `$member` per org is correct for ACLs; it is not a replacement for the global user identity required by DMs, App Home, approvals, and pre-org install claims.

A second issue follows: **sender attribution is not authentication**. Telegram sender minting creates/uses a `person` based on an inbound platform ID. It must never by itself make that person a `$member` or authorize actions. The current Slack adopter is safe specifically because it requires provider-signed identity and only takes over from `person`: `auth/subject-identities.ts:75-154`.

No project files were changed. Current worktree has pre-existing unrelated changes/untracked files; `git diff --stat origin/main...HEAD` is empty.
